𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-cylinders over smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered affine surfacesThanks: The author thanks the organizers of the Kinosaki Algebraic Geometry Symposium for their generous support and the very stimulating discussions held in a warm and friendly atmosphere during this conference.

Adrien Dubouloz Address: IMB UMR5584, CNRS, Univ. Bourgogne Franche-Comté, F-21000 Dijon, France. Email address: adrien.dubouloz@u-bourgogne.fr
Abstract.

We give a general structure theorem for affine 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations on smooth quasi-projective surfaces. As an application, we show that every smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered affine surface non-isomorphic to the total space of a line bundle over a smooth affine curve fails the Zariski Cancellation Problem. The present note is an expanded version of a talk given at the Kinosaki Algebraic Geometry Symposium in October 2019.

Introduction

The Zariski Cancellation Problem asks under which circumstances the existence of a biregular isomorphism between the cartesian products X×𝔸nX\times\mathbb{A}^{n} and Y×𝔸nY\times\mathbb{A}^{n} of two algebraic varieties XX and YY with the affine space 𝔸n\mathbb{A}^{n}, say over a an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, implies that the varieties XX and YY are isomorphic. Cancellation is known to hold for smooth curves [1] and for a large class of algebraic varieties characterized roughly by the property that they are not dominantly covered by images of the affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} (see e.g. [18], [5]). A specific stronger characterization due to Makar-Limanov [2] asserts that if XX is an affine variety which does not admit any effective algebraic action of the additive group 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} then every isomorphism X×𝔸1≃Y×𝔸1X\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\simeq Y\times\mathbb{A}^{1} induces an isomorphism X≃YX\simeq Y (this is no longer true for products with affine spaces 𝔸n\mathbb{A}^{n} of higher dimension, see e.g. [9, 10]).

Among smooth affine surfaces with an effective action of the additive group 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}, cancellation is known to hold for the affine plane 𝔸2\mathbb{A}^{2} by [23, 25]. The first celebrated examples of smooth affine surfaces with effective 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions which fail cancellation were constructed by Danielewski [4]: he established that the smooth surfaces SnS_{n} in 𝔸3\mathbb{A}^{3} defined by the equations xn​z=y⁡(y−1)x^{n}z=y(y-1), where n≥1n\geq 1, are pairwise non-isomorphic but that their 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-cylinders Sn×𝔸1S_{n}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} are all isomorphic. Since then, many other families of examples of smooth affine surfaces with effective 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions which fail cancellation have been constructed (see e.g. [26, 13] and the references therein for a survey). All these constructions are derived from variants of the nowadays called “Danielewski fiber product trick”, which depends on the study of the structure of the algebraic quotient morphisms of 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-actions on affine surfaces. These quotient morphisms are surjections π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C onto smooth affine curves, with generic fiber isomorphic to the affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} over the function field of CC, called 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations. The local structure of these fibrations in a neighborhood of their degenerate fibers has been studied by many authors after the pioneering work of Miyanishi [24] and Fieseler [12]. The first result presented in this note is a general structure theorem for affine 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations on smooth quasi-projective surfaces which generalizes and encompasses, in a different language, all formerly known descriptions:

Theorem.

Let SS be a smooth quasi-projective surface and let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an affine 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration over a smooth algebraic curve CC. Then there exists a smooth algebraic space 𝒞\mathcal{C} of dimension 11 endowed with a surjective quasi-finite birational morphism of finite type α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C and a factorization

π=α∘ρ:S→ρ𝒞→αC\pi=\alpha\circ\rho:S\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\rho}}{{\rightarrow}}\mathcal{C}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\alpha}}{{\rightarrow}}C

where ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is an étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle.

In the case of a smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C on a smooth affine surface SS, the above result was already established in [12] and [7] (see also [13]) with the additional observation that in this particular case, the algebraic space curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C is a smooth scheme, in general not separated. We will see below that for non-smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations, the existence of multiple fibers forces to consider algebraic space curves α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C which are not schemes. This fact was already observed in [9, 10] where the existence of a factorization as above was established for some particular examples of 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations with multiple fibers.

Our second result is an application of the above structure theorem to the construction of smooth affine surfaces which fail cancellation. By applying a new variant of the Danielwski fiber product trick construction, we obtain the following characterization which basically fully settles the Zariski Cancellation Problem for smooth affine surfaces:

Theorem.

Let SS be a smooth affine surface and let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration over a smooth affine curve CC. Then the following alternative holds:

a) If π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is isomorphic to the structure morphism of a line bundle over CC then every smooth affine surface S′S^{\prime} such that S′×𝔸1≃S×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\simeq S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} is isomorphic to SS.

b) Otherwise, there exists a smooth affine 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surface S′S^{\prime} non-isomorphic to SS such that S×𝔸1S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} is isomorphic to S′×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}.

The characterization in the above theorem strongly overlaps similar results established in [13] for smooth surfaces which admit 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations with reduced fibers. We also refer the reader to a forthcoming article in collaboration S. Kaliman and M. Zaidenberg in which a similar result is established by different methods.

In this note, all schemes and algebraic spaces are assumed to be defined for simplicity over the field of complex numbers ℂ\mathbb{C}. We refer the reader to [20] for the basic properties of algebraic spaces which are used throughout the text. Some of the results in this note are given without complete and detailed proofs, these will appear elsewhere.

1. Smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surfaces as étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundles

Definition 1.

An 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS is a surjective affine morphism π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C to a smooth algebraic curve CC, whose fiber over the generic point of CC is isomorphic to the affine line 𝔸K⁡(C)1\mathbb{A}_{K(C)}^{1} over the function field K⁡(C)K(C) of CC.

An 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS is said to be of affine type (resp. complete type) if the curve CC is affine (resp. complete).

Example 2.

Given a smooth algebraic curve CC, a ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}-bundle π¯:ℙ⁡(E)→C\overline{\pi}:\mathbb{P}(E)\rightarrow C for some vector bundle EE of rank 22 on CC and a section σ:C→ℙ⁡(E)\sigma:C\rightarrow\mathbb{P}(E) of π¯\overline{\pi}, the restriction π:S=ℙ⁡(E)∖σ⁡(C)→C\pi:S=\mathbb{P}(E)\setminus\sigma(C)\rightarrow C of π¯\overline{\pi} to the complement of σ⁡(C)\sigma(C) is an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration which is a Zariski locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle over CC, that is, there exists a covering of CC by Zariski open susbets CiC_{i}, i∈Ii\in I, and isomorphisms π−1​(Ci)≃Ci×𝔸1\pi^{-1}(C_{i})\simeq C_{i}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} of schemes over CiC_{i} for every i∈Ii\in I.

If CC is affine, such Zariski locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C are simply line bundles. This is no longer the case in general when CC is complete. For instance, let S⊂𝔸3S\subset\mathbb{A}^{3} be the smooth affine quadric surface with equation x​z=y2−1xz=y^{2}-1. Then the morphism

π:S→ℙ1,(x,y,z)↦[x:y−1]=[y+1:z]\pi:S\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^{1},\quad(x,y,z)\mapsto[x:y-1]=[y+1:z]

is a Zariski locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle which cannot be a line bundle. Indeed, otherwise the zero section of this line bundle would be a complete curve contained in SS, which is impossible as SS is affine.

Proposition 3.

[19, Lemma 1.3] Let SS be a smooth quasi-projective surface and let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration onto a smooth curve CC. Assume that all scheme-theoretic fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C are irreducible and reduced. Then π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is Zariski locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle.

Definition 4.

Let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS. A scheme-theoretic fiber of π\pi over a closed point cc of CC which is either reducible or non-reduced is called degenerate.

By [24, Lemma 1.4.2], every degenerate fiber of an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is a disjoint union of curves isomorphic to the complex affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} when endowed with respective reduced structures.

Example 5.

Let n≥2n\geq 2, let P⁡(y)=∏i=1r(y−yi)mi∈ℂ⁡[y]P(y)=\prod_{i=1}^{r}(y-y_{i})^{m_{i}}\in\mathbb{C}[y] be a non-constant monic polynomial with r≥1r\geq 1 distinct roots yi∈ℂy_{i}\in\mathbb{C} of respective multiplicities mi≥1m_{i}\geq 1 and let S⊂𝔸3S\subset\mathbb{A}^{3} be the affine surface defined by the equation xn​z=P⁡(y)−xx^{n}z=P(y)-x. Then SS is smooth by the Jacobian criterion and the projection prx\mathrm{pr}_{x} induces an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:S→𝔸1\pi:S\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1} which restricts to the trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle 𝔸1∖{0}×Spec⁡(ℂ⁡[y])\mathbb{A}^{1}\setminus\{0\}\times\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{C}[y]) over 𝔸1∖{0}=Spec⁡(ℂ⁡[x±1])\mathbb{A}^{1}\setminus\{0\}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{C}[x^{\pm 1}]). On the other hand, the scheme-theoretic fiber π−1​({0})\pi^{-1}(\{0\}) decomposes as the disjoint union of the schemes

Fi=Spec(ℂ[y]/((y−yi)mi[z]),i=1,…,rF_{i}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{C}[y]/((y-y_{i})^{m_{i}}[z]),\quad i=1,\ldots,r

whose reductions are all isomorphic to the affine line 𝔸1=Spec⁡(ℂ⁡[z])\mathbb{A}^{1}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{C}[z]).

1.1. The smooth relatively connected quotient of an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration

In this subsection, we show that every 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS factors through a smooth morphism with connected fibers ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} over a suitably defined algebraic space curve 𝒞\mathcal{C} over CC.

Definition 6.

Let CC be a smooth algebraic curve. A smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve is a smooth algebraic space 𝒞\mathcal{C} of dimension 11 endowed with a surjective quasi-finite birational morphism of finite type α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C such that α∗​𝒪𝒞=𝒪C\alpha_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}}=\mathcal{O}_{C}.

By generic smoothness, there exists a non empty maximal Zariski open subset UU of CC over which α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C restricts to an étale morphism α:α−1​(U)→U\alpha:\alpha^{-1}(U)\rightarrow U. Given any separated open subset 𝒱⊂α−1​(U)\mathcal{V}\subset\alpha^{-1}(U), the restriction α|𝒱:𝒱→C\alpha|_{\mathcal{V}}:\mathcal{V}\rightarrow C is a separated birational quasi-finite étale morphism. Since a quasi-finite morphism is quasi-affine, 𝒱\mathcal{V} is thus a quasi-projective scheme and α|𝒱:𝒱→C\alpha|_{\mathcal{V}}:\mathcal{V}\rightarrow C is an open immersion by Zariski main theorem [15, Théorème 8.12.6]. It follows in particular that there exists finitely many points c1,…,csc_{1},\ldots,c_{s} of CC over which α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C is not an isomorphism. Furthermore, for every i=1,…,si=1,\ldots,s, the fiber α−1​(ci)\alpha^{-1}(c_{i}) consists of finitely many points c˘i,1,…,c˘i,ri\breve{c}_{i,1},\ldots,\breve{c}_{i,r_{i}}, and if α\alpha is unramified at c˘i,j\breve{c}_{i,j} then there exists a separated Zariski open neighborhood U˘i,j\breve{U}_{i,j} of c˘i,j\breve{c}_{i,j} in 𝒞\mathcal{C} such that α|U˘i,j:U˘i,j→C\alpha|_{\breve{U}_{i,j}}:\breve{U}_{i,j}\rightarrow C is an isomorphism onto its image. So one can picture a smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C as being obtained from the curve CC by “replacing” finitely many points c1,…,csc_{1},\ldots,c_{s} of CC by a collection of finitely many distinct algebraic space curve points c˘i,1,…,c˘i,ri\breve{c}_{i,1},\ldots,\breve{c}_{i,r_{i}}.

Example 7.

Let CC be smooth affine curve, let c0∈Cc_{0}\in C be a closed point and let 𝒞\mathcal{C} be the curve obtained by gluing r≥2r\geq 2 copies αi:𝒞i→≃C\alpha_{i}:\mathcal{C}_{i}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\simeq}}{{\rightarrow}}C, i=1,…,ri=1,\ldots,r, of CC by the identity outside the points ci=αi−1​(c0)c_{i}=\alpha_{i}^{-1}(c_{0}). The curve 𝒞\mathcal{C} is a non-separated scheme on which the morphisms αi\alpha_{i} glue to a surjective quasi-finite birational morphism α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C which coincides with the canonical affinization morphism 𝒞→Spec⁡(Γ⁡(𝒞,𝒪𝒞))\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(\Gamma(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}})). The restriction of α\alpha over C∖{c0}C\setminus\{c_{0}\} is an isomorphism whereas α−1​(c0)\alpha^{-1}(c_{0}) consists of rr distinct point cic_{i}, i=1,…,ri=1,\ldots,r.

Example 8.

Let CC be a smooth algebraic curve, let c0∈Cc_{0}\in C be a closed point and let φ:C~→C\varphi:\tilde{C}\rightarrow C be a quasi-finite morphism of degree m≥2m\geq 2, with branching index mm at cc and étale elsewhere. Let c~0=φ−1​(c0)\tilde{c}_{0}=\varphi^{-1}(c_{0}) and let 𝒞\mathcal{C} be the smooth algebraic space obtained from C~\tilde{C} by identifying two points c~,c~′∈C~∖{c~0}\tilde{c},\tilde{c}^{\prime}\in\tilde{C}\setminus\{\tilde{c}_{0}\} if φ⁡(c~)=φ⁡(c~′)\varphi(\tilde{c})=\varphi(\tilde{c}^{\prime}). More rigorously, letting C∗=C∖{c}C_{*}=C\setminus\{c\} and C~∗=C~∖{c~0}=φ−1​(C∗)\tilde{C}_{*}=\tilde{C}\setminus\{\tilde{c}_{0}\}=\varphi^{-1}(C_{*}), 𝒞\mathcal{C} is the quotient of C~\tilde{C} by the étale equivalence relation

R=Diag⊔j:C~⊔C~∗×C∗C~∗⟶C~×CC~,R=\mathrm{Diag}\sqcup j:\tilde{C}\sqcup\tilde{C}_{*}\times_{C_{*}}\tilde{C}_{*}\longrightarrow\tilde{C}\times_{C}\tilde{C},

where Diag:C~→C~×CC~\mathrm{Diag}:\tilde{C}\rightarrow\tilde{C}\times_{C}\tilde{C} is the diagonal morphism and j:C~∗×C∗C~∗→C~×CC~j:\tilde{C}_{*}\times_{C_{*}}\tilde{C}_{*}\rightarrow\tilde{C}\times_{C}\tilde{C} is the natural open immersion. The RR-invariant morphism φ:C~→C\varphi:\tilde{C}\rightarrow C descends through the quotient morphism q:C~→𝒞=C~/Rq:\tilde{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}=\tilde{C}/R to a bijective quasi-finite morphism α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C restricting to an isomorphism over C∗C_{*}. On the other hand, the inverse image of c0c_{0} by α\alpha consists of a unique point 𝔠0=q⁡(c~0)\mathfrak{c}_{0}=q(\tilde{c}_{0}), at which α\alpha ramification index mm. The sheaf α∗​𝒪𝒞\alpha_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}} is equal to the 𝒪C\mathcal{O}_{C}-submodule of φ∗​𝒪C~\varphi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{C}} consisting of germs of RR-invariant regular functions on C~\tilde{C}, hence is equal to 𝒪C\mathcal{O}_{C}. Since RR is not a locally closed immmersion in a neighborhood of the point c~0∈C~\tilde{c}_{0}\in\tilde{C}, it follows that the algebraic space 𝒞\mathcal{C} is not locally separated in a neighborhood of the point 𝔠0\mathfrak{c}_{0}, hence is not a scheme.

Theorem 9.

Let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projective surface. Then there exists a smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C unique up to CC-isomorphism and a smooth affine morphism with connected fibers ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} such that π=α∘ρ\pi=\alpha\circ\rho.

Sketch of proof.

A smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C with the desired properties is obtained as follows. Let c1,…,csc_{1},\ldots,c_{s} be the points over which the fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C are degenerate and let α˘:C˘→C\breve{\alpha}:\breve{C}\rightarrow C be the scheme obtained from CC as in Example 7 by replacing each point csc_{s} by distinct scheme points c˘i,1,…,c˘i,ri\breve{c}_{i,1},\ldots,\breve{c}_{i,r_{i}}, one for each connected component Fi,jF_{i,j} of the fiber π−1​(ci)\pi^{-1}(c_{i}), i=1,…,si=1,\ldots,s. The unique morphism ρ˘:S→C˘\breve{\rho}:S\rightarrow\breve{C} defined by

ρ˘​(s)={α˘−1​(π​(s))if ​π−1​(π⁡(s))​ is connectedc˘i,jif π⁡(s)=ci​ and ​s∈Fi,j \breve{\rho}(s)=\begin{cases}\breve{\alpha}^{-1}(\pi(s))&\textrm{if }\pi^{-1}(\pi(s))\textrm{ is connected}\\ \breve{c}_{i,j}&\textrm{if }\text{$\pi(s)=c_{i}\textrm{ and }s\in F_{i,j}$ }\end{cases}

is affine with connected fibers and satisfies π=α˘∘ρ˘\pi=\breve{\alpha}\circ\breve{\rho}. Since SS is smooth and every connected component of a fiber of π\pi is irreducible and smooth when equipped with its reduced structure, we see that ρ˘:S→C˘\breve{\rho}:S\rightarrow\breve{C} is smooth over a point c˘\breve{c} of C˘\breve{C} if and only if ρ˘−1​(c˘)\breve{\rho}^{-1}(\breve{c}) is a reduced irreducible component of π−1​(α˘​(c˘))\pi^{-1}(\breve{\alpha}(\breve{c})).

Let c˘0∈C˘\breve{c}_{0}\in\breve{C} be a point such that ρ˘−1​(c˘0)=m​F\breve{\rho}^{-1}(\breve{c}_{0})=mF, where F≃𝔸1F\simeq\mathbb{A}^{1}, is multiple, of multiplicity m≥2m\geq 2 and let ss be a closed point of SS supported on FF. Since SS and FF are smooth at ss, there exists a germ of smooth curve C~0↪S\tilde{C}_{0}\hookrightarrow S intersecting FF transversally at ss. The restriction φ=ρ˘|C~0:C~0→C˘\varphi=\breve{\rho}|_{\tilde{C}_{0}}:\tilde{C}_{0}\rightarrow\breve{C} is quasi-finite onto its image. By shrinking C~0\tilde{C}_{0} if necessary we can assume without loss generality that the image of φ\varphi is an affine open neighborhood C0C_{0} of c˘0\breve{c}_{0} in C˘\breve{C} with the property that π−1​(α˘​(c˘0))\pi^{-1}(\breve{\alpha}(\breve{c}_{0})) is the unique degenerate fiber of π\pi over α˘​(C0)\breve{\alpha}(C_{0}) and that φ:C~0→C0\varphi:\tilde{C}_{0}\rightarrow C_{0} is a quasi-finite morphism of degree m≥2m\geq 2, with ramification index mm at ss and étale elsewhere. Let βc˘0:C~0/R→C0\beta_{\breve{c}_{0}}:\tilde{C}_{0}/R\rightarrow C_{0} be the algebraic space curve over C0C_{0} determined by φ:C~0→C0\varphi:\tilde{C}_{0}\rightarrow C_{0} as in Example 8 and let αc˘0:𝒞c˘0→C˘\alpha_{\breve{c}_{0}}:\mathcal{C}_{\breve{c}_{0}}\rightarrow\breve{C} be the algebraic space curve over C˘\breve{C} obtained by gluing C˘∖{c˘0}\breve{C}\setminus\{\breve{c}_{0}\} with C~0/R\tilde{C}_{0}/R with by the identity along the open subsets C0∖{c˘0}C_{0}\setminus\{\breve{c}_{0}\} and βc˘0−1​(C0∖{c˘0})≃C0∖{c˘0}\beta_{\breve{c}_{0}}^{-1}(C_{0}\setminus\{\breve{c}_{0}\})\simeq C_{0}\setminus\{\breve{c}_{0}\} of C˘∖{c˘0}\breve{C}\setminus\{\breve{c}_{0}\} and C~0/R\tilde{C}_{0}/R respectively. Letting 𝔠0=αc˘0−1​(c˘0)\mathfrak{c}_{0}=\alpha_{\breve{c}_{0}}^{-1}(\breve{c}_{0}), one checks locally on an étale cover of SS that ρ˘:S→C˘\breve{\rho}:S\rightarrow\breve{C} factors through an affine morphism ρc˘0:S→𝒞c˘0\rho_{\breve{c}_{0}}:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C}_{\breve{c}_{0}} smooth over a Zariski open neighborhood of 𝔠0\mathfrak{c}_{0} and such that ρc˘0−1​(𝔠0)=F\rho_{\breve{c}_{0}}^{-1}(\mathfrak{c}_{0})=F. By repeating the above construction for each of the finitely many points of C˘\breve{C} over which the fiber of ρ˘\breve{\rho} is multiple, we obtain a smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C and a smooth affine morphism with connected fibers ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} factoring π\pi.

By construction, for every closed point c∈Cc\in C, the fibers of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} over the points in α−1​(c)\alpha^{-1}(c) are in one-to-one correspondence with the connected components of the fiber of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C over cc. Therefore, if α′:𝒞′→C\alpha^{\prime}:\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\rightarrow C is another smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve with the same properties then its associated smooth morphism ρ′:S→𝒞′\rho^{\prime}:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} is locally constant on the fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C hence constant on the fibers of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C}. This implies in turn by faithfully flat descent that there exists a unique morphism φ:𝒞→𝒞′\varphi:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} of algebraic spaces over CC such that ρ′=φ∘ρ\rho^{\prime}=\varphi\circ\rho. Reversing the roles of 𝒞\mathcal{C} and 𝒞′\mathcal{C}^{\prime}, we conclude that φ\varphi is a CC-isomorphism. ∎

Definition 10.

Let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS. The smooth multifold algebraic space CC-curve α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C such that π\pi factors as π=α∘ρ\pi=\alpha\circ\rho for some smooth affine morphism ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} with connected fibers is called the smooth relatively connected quotient of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C.

It follows from the proof of Theorem 9 that the isomorphism type of α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C as a space over CC depends only on the irreducible components, taken with their respective multiplicities of the scheme-theoretic degenerate fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C.

1.2. Illustration on a toy local model

Let CC be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring 𝒪\mathcal{O} with maximal ideal 𝔪\mathfrak{m} and residue field ℂ\mathbb{C} and let t∈𝔪t\in\mathfrak{m} be a uniformizing parameter. Given integers n,m≥2n,m\geq 2, let Sn,mS_{n,m} be the smooth affine surface in C×𝔸2C\times\mathbb{A}^{2} defined by the equation tn​z=ym−tt^{n}z=y^{m}-t. 1.3. 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations as torsors under étale locally trivial line bundles

Let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration on a smooth quasi-projetive surface, let α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C be its smooth relatively connected quotient and let ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} be the corresponding smooth affine morphism with connected fibers. For every étale morphism f:B→𝒞f:B\rightarrow\mathcal{C} from a smooth algebraic curve BB, the projection prB:S×𝒞B→B\mathrm{pr}_{B}:S\times_{\mathcal{C}}B\rightarrow B is a smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration with connected fibers, hence is a Zariski locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle by virtue of Proposition 3. It follows that ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is an étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle over 𝒞\mathcal{C}. Summing-up, we obtain:

Theorem 11.

Every 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C on a smooth quasi-projective surface SS decomposes as an étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} over a smooth multifold algebraic CC-space curve 𝒞\mathcal{C} followed by the structure morphism α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C of 𝒞\mathcal{C}.

Since the automorphism group of the affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} is the affine group Aff1=𝔾m⋉𝔾a\mathrm{Aff}_{1}=\mathbb{G}_{m}\ltimes\mathbb{G}_{a}, every étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is an étale affine-linear bundle, isomorphic to the associated fiber bundle V×Aff1𝔸1→𝒞V\times^{\mathrm{Aff}_{1}}\mathbb{A}^{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} of a principal homogeneous Aff1\mathrm{Aff}_{1}-bundle V→𝒞V\rightarrow\mathcal{C} over 𝒞\mathcal{C}. It follows that there exists a uniquely determined étale locally trivial line bundle p:LS/𝒞→𝒞p:L_{S/\mathcal{C}}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}, considered as a locally constant group scheme over 𝒞\mathcal{C} for the group law induced by the addition of germs of sections, such that ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} can be further equipped with the structure of an étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor, that is, a principal homogeneous bundle under the action of LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}. Namely, the class of LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}} in the Picard group Pic⁡(𝒞)=He´​t1​(𝒞,𝔾m)\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{C})=H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{m}) of 𝒞\mathcal{C} coincides with the image of the isomorphism class of V→𝒞V\rightarrow\mathcal{C} in He´​t1​(𝒞,Aff1)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},\mathrm{Aff}_{1}) by the map He´​t1​(𝒞,Aff1)→He´​t1​(𝒞,𝔾m)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},\mathrm{Aff}_{1})\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{m}) in the long exact sequence of non-abelian cohomology

⋯→H0​(𝒞,𝔾m)→He´​t1​(𝒞,𝔾a)→He´​t1​(𝒞,Aff1)→He´​t1​(𝒞,𝔾m)\cdots\rightarrow H^{0}\left(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{m}\right)\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}\left(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{a}\right)\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}\left(\mathcal{C},\mathrm{Aff}_{1}\right)\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}\left(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{m}\right)

associated to the short exact sequence 0→𝔾a→Aff1→𝔾m→00\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{a}\rightarrow\mathrm{Aff}_{1}\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow 0 of étale sheaves of groups on 𝒞\mathcal{C}. Isomorphism classes of étale torsors under a given étale locally trivial line bundle p:L→𝒞p:L\rightarrow\mathcal{C} are in turn classified by the cohomology group He´​t1​(𝒞,L)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L) (see e.g. [17, XI.4] or [14, III.2.4]).

The line bundle p:LS/𝒞→𝒞p:L_{S/\mathcal{C}}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} associated to a given étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} can be alternatively described as follows: since ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is an étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle, the pull-back homomorphism

ρ∗:He´​t1​(𝒞,𝔾m)→He´​t1​(S,𝔾m)≃Pic⁡(S)\rho^{*}:H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},\mathbb{G}_{m})\rightarrow H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(S,\mathbb{G}_{m})\simeq\mathrm{Pic}(S)

The same local description as in [16, 16.4.7] then implies that LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}} is the unique étale line bundle on 𝒞\mathcal{C} whose image by ρ∗\rho^{*} is equal to the relative tangent line bundle TS/𝒞=Spec⁡(Sym⋅​ΩS/𝒞)→ST_{S/\mathcal{C}}=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathrm{Sym}^{\cdot}\Omega_{S/\mathcal{C}})\rightarrow S of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C}, where ΩS/𝒞\Omega_{S/\mathcal{C}} denotes the sheaf of relative Kähler differentials of SS over 𝒞\mathcal{C}.

Example 12.

Let Q⊂ℙ2Q\subset\mathbb{P}^{2} be a smooth plane conic. 𝔸1∖{0}∋u∼−u∈𝔸1∖{0}.\mathbb{A}^{1}\setminus\{0\}\ni u\sim-u\in\mathbb{A}^{1}\setminus\{0\}.

Let ρ1:S1→𝒞\rho_{1}:S_{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} and ρn,2:Sn,2→𝒞\rho_{n,2}:S_{n,2}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} be the étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundles factoring π1\pi_{1} and πn,2\pi_{n,2} respectively. 2. 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-cylinders of smooth 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surfaces of affine type

Given a smooth quasi-projective 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surface π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C with smooth relatively connected quotient α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C, the isomorphism class of SS as a scheme over 𝒞\mathcal{C} is determined by the pair consisting of the isomorphism class in Pic⁡(𝒞)\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{C}) of the étale line bundle p:LS/𝒞→𝒞p:L_{S/\mathcal{C}}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} under which the associated étale locally trivial 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundle ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is an LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor and of the isomorphism class of this torsor in He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}). In contrast, the following results shows in particular that when CC is an affine curve, the isomorphism class as scheme over 𝒞\mathcal{C} of the cylinder S×𝔸1S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} over SS is independent of the class of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} in He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}).

Theorem 13.

Let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C and π′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C be smooth quasi-projective 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surfaces over a same affine curve CC. Let α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C and α′:𝒞′→C\alpha^{\prime}:\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\rightarrow C be their respective smooth relatively connected quotients and let ρ:S→𝒞′\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} and ρ′:S′→𝒞′\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} be the associated étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor and LS′/𝒞′L_{S^{\prime}/\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}-torsor respectively.

Then the threefolds S×𝔸1S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} and S′×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} are isomorphic as schemes over CC if and only if there exists a CC-isomorphism ψ:𝒞→𝒞′\psi:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} such that ψ∗​LS′/𝒞′≃LS/𝒞\psi^{*}L_{S^{\prime}/\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}\simeq L_{S/\mathcal{C}}.

Proof.

A CC-isomorphism Ψ:S×𝔸1→≃S′×𝔸1\Psi:S\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\simeq}}{{\rightarrow}}S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} induces for each closed point c∈Cc\in C a multiplicity preserving one-to-one correspondence between the irreducible components of the fiber of π∘prS\pi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S} over cc and the irreducible components of the fiber of π′∘prS′\pi^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}} over cc. It follows from the construction of the smooth relatively connected quotients α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C and α′:𝒞′→C\alpha^{\prime}:\mathcal{C}^{\prime}\rightarrow C that Ψ\Psi induces a CC-isomorphism ψ:𝒞→𝒞′\psi:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} such that ψ∘(ρ∘prS)=(ρ′∘prS′)∘Ψ\psi\circ(\rho\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S})=(\rho^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}})\circ\Psi. Since the morphisms ρ∘prS:S×𝔸1→𝒞\rho\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S}:S\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} and ρ′∘prS′:S′×𝔸1→𝒞′\rho^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}}:S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^{\prime} are étale locally trivial 𝔸2\mathbb{A}^{2}-bundles over 𝒞\mathcal{C} and 𝒞′\mathcal{C}^{\prime} respectively, the pull-back homomorphisms

(ρ∘prS)∗:Pic⁡(𝒞)→Pic⁡(S×𝔸1)and(ρ′∘prS′)∗:Pic⁡(𝒞′)→Pic⁡(S′×𝔸1)(\rho\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S})^{*}:\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{C})\rightarrow\mathrm{Pic}(S\times\mathbb{A}^{1})\quad\textrm{and}\quad(\rho^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}})^{*}:\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{C}^{\prime})\rightarrow\mathrm{Pic}(S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1})

are both isomorphisms. Let TS×𝔸1/𝒞T_{S\times\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathcal{C}} and TS′×𝔸1/𝒞′T_{S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathcal{C}^{\prime}} be the relative tangent bundles of the morphisms ρ∘prS\rho\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S} and ρ′∘prS′\rho^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}} respectively. By definition of LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}} and LS′/𝒞′L_{S^{\prime}/\mathcal{C}^{\prime}} (see subsection 1.3), we have

from which it follows that LS/𝒞≃ψ∗​LS′/𝒞′L_{S/\mathcal{C}}\simeq\psi^{*}L_{S^{\prime}/\mathcal{C}^{\prime}}.

Remark 14.

The proof of Theorem 13 depends in a crucial way on the existence of an étale 𝔾a,𝒞\mathbb{G}_{a,\mathcal{C}}-torsor ρ0:S0→𝒞\rho_{0}:S_{0}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} with affine total space S0S_{0}. Such a torsor does not exist in general if the curve CC is not affine. For instance, if 𝒞=C=ℙ1\mathcal{C}=C=\mathbb{P}^{1}, the vanishing of H1​(ℙ1,𝒪ℙ1)H^{1}(\mathbb{P}^{1},\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{1}}) implies that the only 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-torsor over ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1} is the trivial one ℙ1×𝔸1\mathbb{P}^{1}\times\mathbb{A}^{1} on which 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a} acts by translations on second factor, whose total space is not affine. Similiarly, if 𝒞=C\mathcal{C}=C is a smooth elliptic curve, then the total space of the unique non-trivial 𝔾a\mathbb{G}_{a}-torsor ρ0:S0→C\rho_{0}:S_{0}\rightarrow C corresponding to the unique non-trivial extension

0→𝒪C→ℰ→𝒪C→00\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{C}\rightarrow 0

via the isomorphism Ext1​(𝒪C,𝒪C)≃H1​(C,𝒪C)≃ℂ\mathrm{Ext}^{1}(\mathcal{O}_{C},\mathcal{O}_{C})\simeq H^{1}(C,\mathcal{O}_{C})\simeq\mathbb{C} is a quasi-projective surface which is not affine.

Example 15.

Consider again the smooth affine surfaces Sn,2S_{n,2} in 𝔸3\mathbb{A}^{3} defined by the equations xn​z=y2−xx^{n}z=y^{2}-x, n≥2n\geq 2. By Example 12, each of these surfaces is an étale torsor ρn,2:Sn,2→𝒞\rho_{n,2}:S_{n,2}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} under the tangent line bundle T𝒞T_{\mathcal{C}} of the multifold algebraic space curve α:𝒞→𝔸1\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1} obtained as the quotient of the affine line with a double origin by a free μ2\mu_{2}-action. One can check that up to composition by automorphisms of 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}, πn,2=prx|Sn,2:Sn,2→𝔸1\pi_{n,2}=\mathrm{pr}_{x}|_{S_{n,2}}:S_{n,2}\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1} is the unique 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration of affine type on Sn,2S_{n,2}. Combined with the fact that the étale 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundles ρn,2:Sn,2→𝒞\rho_{n,2}:S_{n,2}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} are pairwise non-isomorphic, this implies that the surfaces Sn,2S_{n,2} are pairwise non-isomorphic as abstract varieties. On the other hand, it follows from Theorem 13 that the cylinders Sn,2×𝔸1S_{n,2}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}, n≥2n\geq 2, are all isomorphic. We thus recover a particular case of non-cancellation for so-called affine pseudo-planes studied in [22].

We conclude with the following theorem which provides a complete answer to the cancellation problem for smooth affine surfaces admitting 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibrations of affine type.

Theorem 16.

Let SS be a smooth affine surface and let π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C be an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration over a smooth affine curve CC. Then the following alternative holds:

a) If π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is isomorphic to the structure morphism of a line bundle over CC then every smooth affine surface S′S^{\prime} such that S′×𝔸1≃S×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\simeq S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} is isomorphic to SS.

b) Otherwise, there exists a smooth affine 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibered surface S′S^{\prime} non-isomorphic to SS such that S×𝔸1S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} is isomorphic to S′×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}.

Sketch of proof.

Assume that π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is a line bundle, let S′S^{\prime} be a smooth affine surface and let Ψ:S′×𝔸1→≃S×𝔸1\Psi:S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\simeq}}{{\rightarrow}}S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} be an isomorphism of abstract algebraic varieties. If C≃𝔸1C\simeq\mathbb{A}^{1} then π:S→𝔸1\pi:S\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1} is a trivial line bundle so that S≃𝔸2S\simeq\mathbb{A}^{2}. The assertion then follows from [25]. Otherwise, if C≄𝔸1C\not\simeq\mathbb{A}^{1} then since every morphism 𝔸1→C\mathbb{A}^{1}\rightarrow C is constant, it follows that the composition of Ψ\Psi with the projection π∘prS:S×𝔸1→C\pi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S}:S\times\mathbb{A}^{1}\rightarrow C descends to a unique morphism π′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C such that (π∘prS)∘Ψ=π′∘prS′(\pi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S})\circ\Psi=\pi^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}}. Since π∘prS\pi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S} is a Zariski locally trivial 𝔸2\mathbb{A}^{2}-bundle, it follows that the same holds for π′∘prS′\pi^{\prime}\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S^{\prime}}. This implies in turn that π′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C is an 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration without degenerate fibers, hence is a line bundle as CC is affine. Arguing as in the proof of Theorem13, we conclude that π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C and π′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C are isomorphic line bundles over CC, hence that S≃S′S\simeq S^{\prime}.

Now assume that π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C is not isomorphic to the structure morphism of a line bundle over CC. Since CC is affine, it follows that π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C has at least a degenerate fiber. Let α:𝒞→C\alpha:\mathcal{C}\rightarrow C be the smooth relatively connected quotient of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C and let ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} be the associated étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor. Since π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C has a degenerate fiber, it follows from the construction of the smooth relatively connected quotient that 𝒞\mathcal{C} is a non-separated algebraic space or scheme and that α\alpha is not an isomorphism. Since SS is affine, hence is a separated scheme, this implies in particular that ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} is a non-trivial étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor whose isomorphism class in He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}) is thus a non-zero element.

Let ℒ\mathcal{L} be the étale invertible sheaf of germs of section of LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}} and let ff be a non-zero regular function on CC. The multiplication by α∗​f\alpha^{*}f defines an injective homomorphism s:ℒ→ℒs:\mathcal{L}\rightarrow\mathcal{L} which determines in turn a non-zero homomorphism of group schemes ζ:LS/𝒞→LS/𝒞\zeta:L_{S/\mathcal{C}}\rightarrow L_{S/\mathcal{C}}. Arguing as in the proof of Theorem 13, we can find an étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsor ρ′:S′→𝒞\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} with affine total space and an ss-equivariant 𝒞\mathcal{C}-morphism ξ:S′→S\xi:S^{\prime}\rightarrow S of torsors with the property that the isomorphism class of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} in He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}) is the image by H1​(s)H^{1}(s) of the isomorphism class of ρ′:S′→𝒞\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} in He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}).

We claim that by choosing f∈Γ⁡(C,𝒪C)f\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal{O}_{C}) appropriately, we can ensure simultaneously that on the one hand the morphism π′=α∘ρ′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}=\alpha\circ\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C is the unique 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration of affine type on S′S^{\prime} and that on the other hand, for every automorphism ψ\psi of 𝒞\mathcal{C}, the 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-bundles ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} and pr2:S′×ρ′,𝒞,ψ𝒞→𝒞\mathrm{pr}_{2}:S^{\prime}\times_{\rho^{\prime},\mathcal{C},\psi}\mathcal{C}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} are not isomorphic. Indeed, the first condition is automatically satisfied unless CC is isomorphic to the affine line 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}. In the case where C=𝔸1C=\mathbb{A}^{1}, it is enough to choose a regular function ff which vanishes sufficiently at the points of CC over which the fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C are degenerate to ensure the existence of an SNC-minimal projective completion S¯′\overline{S}^{\prime} of S′S^{\prime} whose boundary divisor is not a chain, a property which implies that π′:S′→C\pi^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow C is the unique 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration of affine type on S′S^{\prime} (see e.g. [3, Théorème 1.8] or [6, Theorem 2.16]). Similarly, choosing ff so that it vanishes at the points of CC over which the fibers of π:S→C\pi:S\rightarrow C are degenerate is enough to guarantee that the images of the isomorphism classes of ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} and ρ′:S′→𝒞\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} in ℙ​He´​t1​(𝒞,LS/𝒞)\mathbb{P}H_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}^{1}(\mathcal{C},L_{S/\mathcal{C}}) do not belong the same orbit of the action of the automorphism group of 𝒞\mathcal{C}.

To conclude, one checks that for a regular function ff satisfying the two properties above, the surfaces SS and S′S^{\prime} are not isomorphic as abstract algebraic varieties. On the other hand, since ρ:S→𝒞\rho:S\rightarrow\mathcal{C} and ρ′:S′→𝒞\rho^{\prime}:S^{\prime}\rightarrow\mathcal{C} are both étale LS/𝒞L_{S/\mathcal{C}}-torsors, we deduce from Theorem 13 that S×𝔸1S\times\mathbb{A}^{1} is isomorphic to S′×𝔸1S^{\prime}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}. ∎

ζ:𝔾a,𝔸~1=Spec⁡(𝒪𝔸~1​[t])→Spec⁡(𝒪𝔸~1​[t])=𝔾a,𝔸~1,t↦xn​t\zeta:\mathbb{G}_{a,\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}=\mathrm{\mathrm{Spec}}(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}[t])\rightarrow\mathrm{\mathrm{Spec}}(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}[t])=\mathbb{G}_{a,\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}},\;t\mapsto x^{n}t

It follows that there exists a 𝔾a,𝔸~1\mathbb{G}_{a,\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}-torsor ρn:Sn→𝔸~1\rho_{n}:S_{n}\rightarrow\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1} whose isomorphism class in H1​(𝔸~1,𝒪𝔸~1)H^{1}(\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1},\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}) is equal to the class of the cocyle gng_{n} and a ζ\zeta-equivariant morphism of 𝔾a,𝔸~1\mathbb{G}_{a,\tilde{\mathbb{A}}^{1}}-torsors ξ:Sn→S0\xi:S_{n}\rightarrow S_{0}.

ξ:Sn→S0,(x,y,z)↦(x,y,xn​z).\xi:S_{n}\rightarrow S_{0},\quad(x,y,z)\mapsto(x,y,x^{n}z).

By Theorem 13, the cylinders Sn×𝔸1S_{n}\times\mathbb{A}^{1}, n≥0n\geq 0, are all isomorphic. Clearly, the surface S0S_{0} admits a second 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration of affine type given by the restriction of the projection prz\mathrm{pr}_{z}. On the other hand, for every n≥2n\geq 2, πn:Sn→𝔸1\pi_{n}:S_{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{1} is the unique 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1}-fibration of affine type on SnS_{n} up to composition by automorphisms of 𝔸1\mathbb{A}^{1} (see e.g. [21]). It follows that for every n≥2n\geq 2, SnS_{n} is not isomorphic to S0S_{0}. Actually, the surfaces SnS_{n}, n≥0n\geq 0, are even pairwise non isomorphic [4, 21].
